ledger.x: 1612: the Swedish Empire begins with the reign of Gustavus Adolphus.
The Kalmar War began in April 1611, before this dossier's first year: 'in April 1611,...
Began in July 1611, before this dossier's first year: 'In July 1611, a Swedish expeditionary corps under Jacob De la Gardie captured Novgorod.'
20 January 1613, the Treaty of Knäred: 'All conquests made by both sides are returned', so Kalmar goes back to Sweden; Älvsborg is the exception (next event).

January 1613: Denmark-Norway keeps Älvsborg and Gullberg until Sweden pays the ransom: infobox 'Älvsborg temporarily controlled by Denmark (1613)' and 'Sweden pays 1 million rixdollars as ransom for Älvsborg'.
'the war dragged on until 1614 when the Swedes captured Gdov.'
9 March 1617: the Treaty of Stolbovo gives Sweden Kexholm and Ingria.
9 March 1617, the Treaty of Stolbovo 'restored Novgorod and Gdov which they had occupied since 1611 and 1614, respectively'.
9 March 1617: Gdov is returned at Stolbovo ('restored Novgorod and Gdov').
1619: the Älvsborg pledge ends.
August 1621: 'a Swedish army landed near Pärnu' (19 August 1621); 'Riga capitulated on 25 September' after a siege from 29 August.
November 1622: 'Under the terms of the Truce of Mitawa in November 1622, they ceded Livonia north of the Daugava'; the truce was prolonged to March 1625 and the fighting resumed in 1625.
November 1622: the Truce of Mitawa cedes Livonia north of the Daugava.
1629: Sweden keeps the Prussian coast.

1630: Sweden occupies the duchy: infobox 'Occupied by Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden: 1630'; the Thirty Years' War page has him land 'in Pomerania in June 1630 with nearly 18,000 troops' and the Swedish Empire page has Pomerania 'in its possession since the Treaty of Stettin (1630)'.
April 1632: Swedish armies hold ground in Germany after 'victories at Breitenfeld in September 1631, then Rain in April 1632'.
1635: Sweden gives up the Prussian ports.

1635: 'the German states and Ferdinand agreed to the Peace of Prague' and the Heilbronn and Catholic Leagues 'agreed to dissolve their forces'; after Nördlingen (September 1634) the Swedes hold little of the zone, and Cliopatria's shape drops it in 1636 (Wittstock, October 1636, re-established Swedish predominance…
10 March 1637: 'Death of Duke Bogislaw XIV: 10 March 1637'; 'the last Griffin duke had died during the Thirty Years' War in 1637'.
10 March 1637: the duchy ends and 'was partitioned between Brandenburg-Prussia and Sweden'; Western Pomerania is the part Sweden keeps.
March 1637: Swedish troops hold the rest of the duchy against Brandenburg's inheritance claim.
April 1639: Banér carries the war into Saxony and Bohemia.
December 1642: Leipzig falls.

'in the Danish-Swedish Torstenson War of 1643–1645 the Swedes seized de facto rule in both prince-bishoprics', so 'Frederick II had to resign as Administrator' (he was 'a son of King Christian IV of Denmark and Norway').
As for Bremen: the Swedes 'seized de facto rule in both prince-bishoprics' in the Torstenson War (1643-1645); the Danish administrator Frederick II resigned.
13 August 1645: the Treaty of Brömsebro gives Sweden Gotland and Ösel.
13 August 1645: Jämtland and Härjedalen pass from Norway to Sweden.
13 August 1645: Sweden holds Halland for 30 years.
24 October 1648: the Peace of Westphalia ends the Swedish hold on Saxony and Bohemia; page silent on the evacuation, Cliopatria drops the zone in 1648.
24 October 1648: the Peace of Westphalia ends the Swedish hold on Leipzig and the German zone of the 1640s; page silent on the evacuation.
24 October 1648: Sweden gets Wismar.

24 October 1648: the Peace of Westphalia turns the occupied archbishopric into Swedish territory ('transformed by the Peace of Westphalia in 1648 into the Duchy of Bremen'); the Bremen page's infobox dates the secularisation to 15 May 1648, which prince-archbishopric-of-bremen L11/L12 use, so the neighbour's month…
24 October 1648: Sweden gets the Duchy of Bremen.
24 October 1648: Verden becomes the Swedish Principality of Verden at Westphalia.
24 October 1648: Sweden gets the Principality of Verden.

1653: 'The recess of Stettin in 1653 settled the border with Brandenburg in a manner favourable to Sweden'; Farther Pomerania passes to Brandenburg-Prussia (brandenburg-prussia L6 dates the gain to 1653; swedish-pomerania L7 to 4 May 1653).

21 July 1655: Wittenberg's division 'entered Poland'; 'the nobles surrendered to Wittenberg on 25 July in Ujście' (Greater Poland), 'On 8 September Charles X Gustav occupied Warsaw', 'Kraków surrendered... on 19 October', and Thorn, Elbing and 'Marienburg (Malbork) surrendered in March' 1656.

July 1656: 'a reserve force of the Russian army struck across Swedish Ingria and overran two key Baltic fortresses' (Nöteborg and Nyenschantz); Dorpat 'fell in October'; Daugavpils and Koknese were taken.
1658: 'The Swedish army captured Duke Jacob (1658–1660)'.
8 March 1658: the Treaty of Roskilde turns the Halland pledge into a cession.
8 March 1658: Denmark-Norway cedes Scania, Blekinge, Halland and Bornholm.
8 March 1658: Denmark-Norway cedes Bohuslän and Trøndelag.

23 April 1660, the Treaty of Oliva: 'All occupied territories were restored to their pre-war sovereigns' and 'Sweden was accepted as sovereign in Swedish Livonia'; 'John II Casimir withdrew his claims to the Swedish throne'.
23 April 1660: Oliva restores 'all occupied territories', which for Courland ends the capture of Duke Jacob.
27 May 1660: the Treaty of Copenhagen returns Trøndelag and Bornholm.

2 July 1661, the Treaty of Cardis: the Tsar 'surrendered the Baltic provinces to Sweden'; the war page: Russia was obliged to 'yield its occupied Livonian and Ingrian territories', confirming Stolbovo.
1675: the Scanian War takes Swedish Germany.
29 June 1679: Swedish Germany is restored.
29 June 1679, Saint-Germain: 'Sweden received almost full restitution of its German territory', but Brandenburg kept Gollnow and the strip on the east bank of the Oder.
1703: Ingria falls to Russia.
24 June 1704: 'Marshal Boris Sheremetev's force of 20,000 captured Tartu on 24 June.'
20 August 1704: 'the Russians captured Narva on 20 August 1704'; the city was 'incorporated into the Russian Tsardom' after an oath of 11 September.
1706: Charles XII invades Saxony.
1707: Charles XII leaves Saxony.
1710: Riga and Livonia fall to Russia.
Autumn 1710: Estonia falls to Russia.
1710: Vyborg falls to Russia.
1712: 'In 1712, during the Great Northern War...
1714: Russia occupies Finland, the Great Wrath.

1715: Denmark-Norway ends its occupation by selling the duchies to George I: 'In return for George I's aid, Denmark-Norway sold to him Bremen-Verden, which it kept under occupation since 1712'; the Electorate of Hanover page: 'In 1715, he purchased the duchies of Bremen-Verden from King Frederick IV of Denmark'.
1715: Hanover takes de facto possession by the purchase; Sweden has not ceded it, which happens in 1719.

1715: 'Brandenburg-Prussia openly joined the coalition by declaring war on Sweden in the summer of 1715'; the Swedish Pomerania page: 'The Danes seized Rügen and Western Pomerania north of the Peene River', the areas south of it 'were taken by Prussia'.

Rügen fell in November 1715 ('a combined Danish-Saxon-Prussian army landed at Groß Stresow and took the island of Rügen') and Stralsund on 24 December: 'From 12 July to 24 December 1715, the allies sieged the town and eventually forced its surrender'.
1716: 'Also in 1716, Swedish Wismar surrendered to the allies, eliminating Sweden's last stronghold on the southern Baltic coast'.
1719: Sweden cedes Bremen-Verden: 'Hanover gained Swedish Bremen-Verden' in the treaties of 1719; the Bremen-Verden page: 'the Treaty of Stockholm of 1719'.
1719: Bremen-Verden goes to Hanover.
21 January 1720: the Treaty of Stockholm; 'Prussia had been allowed to retain its conquest, including Stettin'.
21 January 1720: the Treaty of Stockholm with Prussia.
1721: Wismar returns to Sweden; no opened page dates it.

17 January 1721: 'Denmark returned its Pomeranian territories to Swedish administration on 17 January 1721'; the Stralsund page: 'Stralsund remained under Danish control until it was returned to Sweden by the Treaty of Frederiksborg'.
10 September 1721 (30 August O.S.): Finland is given back.
10 September 1721: the Treaty of Nystad confirms the loss of the Baltic provinces.
18 August 1743: the Treaty of Åbo moves the border to the Kymi River.

13 September 1757: Sweden 'invaded Prussian Pomerania' (declaration of war 22 September 1757); the Swedes took Peenemünde, reached Anklam and held Usedom and Wollin until they 'withdrew into Swedish Pomerania' in late 1759, and the war lasted to 1762.

22 May 1762: 'The war was formally ended on 22 May 1762 by the Peace of Hamburg between Prussia, Mecklenburg and Sweden'; 'Prussia and Sweden were restored to the status quo ante bellum', and the infobox lists no territorial change.

1803: 'In 1803, Sweden ceded both the town and lordship to the Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin for 1,258,000 Riksdalers' but 'reserved the right of redemption after 100 years'; Sweden renounced its claim in 1903.
1807: the French occupation of Swedish Pomerania 'beginning in 1807' follows Sweden's entry into the Third Coalition in 1805.

21 February 1808: 'On February 21, 1808, 24,000 Russian troops... crossed the Swedish–Russian border'; Helsinki fell on 2 March, Sveaborg on 6 May, and 'By November 1808, Russian forces had overrun all of Finland'.
17 September 1809: the Treaty of Fredrikshamn turns the occupation into a cession (next event).
17 September 1809: 'in which Sweden ceded the whole of Finland and all of its domains east of the Torne river'.
1810: 'Under the Treaty of Paris, signed in 1810, the territory was returned to Sweden'.
4 November 1814: the Swedish Empire row ends as Sweden and Norway unite.
ledger.cpn: United Kingdoms of Sweden and Norway

wars.name: Ingrian War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Stolbovo, 9 March 1617: Sweden gains Kexholm and Ingria, Novgorod and other gains are returned, Russia renounces Estonia and Livonia.

wars.name: Kalmar War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Knäred, 20 January 1613: all conquests returned, Sweden pays 1 million rixdollars as ransom for Älvsborg, which Denmark-Norway holds meanwhile.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1621-1625)
wars.outcome: Truce of Mitawa, November 1622: the Commonwealth cedes Livonia north of the Daugava; the war resumes in 1625 and Sweden 'now controlled the line of the Daugava'.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1626-1629)
wars.outcome: Truce of Altmark, 26 September 1629: Sweden keeps Livonia down to the Daugava including Riga and the Prussian coastal cities, which it returns in 1635 (Stuhmsdorf).

wars.name: Thirty Years' War
wars.outcome: Peace of Westphalia, 24 October 1648: Sweden gains Western Pomerania, Wolin, Wismar, Bremen-Verden and five million thalers; the armies' other conquests are given up.

wars.name: Torstenson War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Brömsebro, 13 August 1645: Jämtland, Härjedalen, Gotland and Ösel to Sweden, Halland for 30 years, Bremen and Verden under Swedish control.

wars.name: Second Northern War (Polish front)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Oliva, 23 April 1660: 'All occupied territories were restored to their pre-war sovereigns'; Sweden keeps Livonia.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1656-1658)
wars.outcome: Truce of Valiesar, 20 December 1658 (Russia keeps Koknese, Aluksne, Dorpat and Nyslott for three years); Treaty of Cardis, 2 July 1661: Russia yields the occupied Livonian and Ingrian territories.

wars.name: Second Northern War (Danish front)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Roskilde, 8 March 1658: Scania, Blekinge, Halland, Bohuslän, Trøndelag and Bornholm to Sweden; second Swedish attack, Copenhagen attacked, Charles forced to withdraw in 1659; Treaty of Copenhagen, 27 May 1660: Bornholm and Trøndelag returned.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Nystad, 10 September 1721: Sweden loses Estonia, Livonia, Ingria, Kexholm and part of Karelia, keeps Finland; Stockholm 1719-1720: Hanover gets Bremen-Verden, Prussia southern Swedish Pomerania.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1741-1743)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Åbo, 18 August 1743: Sweden cedes the land east of the Kymi River, Villmanstrand and Fredrikshamn; Russia had occupied most of Finland.

wars.name: Pomeranian War
wars.outcome: Peace of Hamburg, 22 May 1762: Prussia and Sweden 'restored to the status quo ante bellum'.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1788-1790)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Värälä, 14 August 1790: status quo ante bellum, 'All conquests made by both sides are returned'.

wars.name: Finnish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Fredrikshamn, 17 September 1809: Sweden cedes Finland, Åland, a part of Lapland and a part of West Bothnia.

wars.name: Swedish-Norwegian war of 1814
wars.outcome: A brief war ended in a ceasefire and the Convention of Moss (August 1814); Norway accepted a personal union, formed on 4 November 1814.

certainty.note: Conquests, truces and army-held German zones; the Lapland and Norwegian frontiers are unsurveyed throughout the empire's life.

Nystad 1721, the Kymi River border of Åbo 1743, Fredrikshamn 1809, Kiel 1814; only the Lapland frontier stays soft.
